💡 Key Takeaways
  • If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
  • The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm.
  • It has been revealed that as it presently stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere.

If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech company and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.

The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Company’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly promptly.

It has been revealed that as it presently stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.".

The concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

NASA pushes Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1248 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, NASA is pushing the limits of helicopter flight on Mars, testing rotor blades at speeds once considered too risky.
  • During tests conducted in March at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, engineers successfully pushed the tips of experimental Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound without causing them to break apart.
  • "NASA had a great run with the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, but we are asking these next-generation aircraft to do even more at the Red Planet," stated Al Chen, Mars Exploration Program manager at JPL.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, NASA is pushing the limits of helicopter flight on Mars, testing rotor blades at speeds once considered too risky. The faster these blades spin, the more lift they can generate, potentially allowing future aircraft to carry heavier scientific instruments and travel greater distances across the Red Planet.

During tests conducted in March at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, engineers successfully pushed the tips of experimental Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound without causing them to break apart. The experiments took place inside a specialized chamber designed to reproduce the harsh atmospheric conditions on Mars. Results from 137 test runs could help engineers develop a new generation of more powerful aircraft capable of carrying scientific equipment.

"NASA had a great run with the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, but we are asking these next-generation aircraft to do even more at the Red Planet," stated Al Chen, Mars Exploration Program manager at JPL. "That's not an easy ask. While everything about Mars is hard, flying there is just about the hardest thing you can do. That's because its atmosphere is so incredibly thin that it is hard to generate lift, and yet Mars has significant gravity.".

According to recent reports, ingenuity made history on April 19, 2021, when it became the first aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another world. However, it was designed primarily to demonstrate that flight on Mars was possible, not to transport scientific instruments. NASA now hopes to go much further. Its recently announced SkyFall project, along with other potential future aircraft, could carry sensors and scientific instruments to investigate Mars from the air. Flying at low altitudes would provide valuable information to support future robotic and human missions.

Why Flying on Mars Requires Extreme Rotor Speeds.

Helicopters generate more thrust by spinning their rotors faster or using blades with a larger diameter. That basic principle applies on Earth and Mars, but the Red Planet presents a much greater engineering challenge.

Mars has an atmosphere only about 1% as dense as Earth's, leaving helicopter blades with far fewer air molecules to push against. To produce enough lift, engineers must operate rotors at exceptionally high speeds, bringing their tips close to the speed of sound. Small rotors on Earth can also spin thousands of times per minute, but the denser atmosphere makes it unnecessary to push their tips toward supersonic speeds to generate substantial lift.

Recent findings suggest that during Ingenuity's 72 flights on Mars, its engineers limited the helicopter's composite-skinned foam rotors to 2,700 revolutions per minute. This restriction served two important purposes. It kept the blades away from the complex and potentially unpredictable conditions near the sound barrier, and it provided a safety margin in case sudden winds (from a dust devil, for instance) caused the blade tips to move faster relative to the surrounding air.

"If Chuck Yeager were here, he'd tell you things can get squirrely around Mach 1," said JPL's Jaakko Karras, the rotor test lead. "With that in mind, we planned Ingenuity's flights to keep the rotor blade tips at Mach 0.7 with no wind so that if we encountered a Martian headwind while in flight, the rotor tips wouldn't go supersonic. But we want more performance from our next-gen Mars aircraft. We needed to know that our rotors could go faster safely.".

According to recent reports, the speed of sound also differs considerably between the two planets. At sea level on Earth, Mach 1 is approximately 760 mph (1,223 kph). On Mars, sound travels at roughly 540 mph (869 kph), largely because the atmosphere is much colder and consists primarily of carbon dioxide.

NASA Tests Supersonic Rotors in a Mars Simulation Chamber.

Industry observers note that to determine whether the new blades could safely reach these extreme speeds, Karras and his colleagues used JPL's historic 25-Foot Space Simulator. The rotor systems were developed and manufactured by AeroVironment in Simi Valley, California.

In a recent development, the researchers began with a three-bladed rotor designed for potential future Mars helicopters. After installing it inside the chamber, they removed the surrounding air and introduced a carefully controlled amount of carbon dioxide to recreate the thin Martian atmosphere. They then spun the rotor at progressively higher speeds while exposing it to simulated winds.

According to recent reports, because the experiment involved the possibility of a rotor breaking apart at supersonic speeds, engineers reinforced part of the chamber with sheet metal. The team monitored the experiment from a control room located just a few yards away, using instruments and a camera to track the rotor's performance.

Industry observers note that the rotor eventually reached 3,750 revolutions per minute, bringing its blade tips to Mach 0.98, just below the speed of sound. Engineers then switched on a fan to produce headwinds against the spinning blades. With each successive test, they increased the wind speed to push the system further.

Breaking the Sound Barrier Boosts Lift by 30%.

In a recent development, the experiments ultimately drove the rotor tips to Mach 1.08, surpassing the sound barrier and increasing the aircraft's lift capability by 30%. Crucially, the blades survived the supersonic conditions.

That additional lift could make a major difference for future missions. More powerful Mars helicopters could transport heavier scientific instruments, advanced sensors, and larger batteries, allowing them to conduct more ambitious investigations and remain airborne for longer periods.

Following the successful tests of the three-bladed design, the team evaluated a second rotor intended for SkyFall. This version has two blades that are slightly longer than those used in the first configuration. Because of their greater length, the blade tips could reach the same near-supersonic speed at a lower rotational rate of 3,570 revolutions per minute before simulated headwinds were introduced.

Industry observers note that "The successful testing of these rotors was a major step toward proving the feasibility of flight in more demanding environments, which is key for next-gen vehicles," noted Shannah Withrow-Maser, an aerodynamicist from NASA's Ames Research Center in Silicon Valley and member of the test team. "We thought we'd be lucky to hit Mach 1.05, and we reached Mach 1.08 on our last runs. We're still digging into the data, and there may be even more thrust on the table. These next-gen helicopters are going to be amazing.".

Next-Generation Mars Helicopters Could Launch in 2028.

Industry observers note that engineers working on SkyFall have already incorporated the latest test results into the project's performance specifications. The findings provide an vital foundation for designing helicopters that can operate under more demanding conditions while carrying substantially more equipment than Ingenuity.

Inspired by the historic success of Ingenuity, which remains the only rotorcraft ever to fly on another planet, SkyFall is designed to transport three next-generation helicopters to Mars in December 2028.

If successfully developed and deployed, these aircraft could expand the possibilities for exploring Mars, providing scientists with a new way to investigate the planet's surface and gather information from locations that may be difficult for traditional rovers to reach.

Materials provided by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It is finally time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5 as we open the doors for Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Now that we are turning to the next chapter, we have to look back on GTA 5 with a fond smile and tearful eyes.
  • GTA 5 had a massive impact on the world, and it is now time to reflect on the game before booting up GTA 6 and moving on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is finally time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5 as we open the doors for Grand Theft Auto 6. This doesn’t mean that we didn’t have some good times with GTA 5, but all good things must eventually come to an end.

Now that we are turning to the next chapter, we have to look back on GTA 5 with a fond smile and tearful eyes. Some of the best memories for people were made with that game. Communities came together, lawsuits were filed, and more.

GTA 5 had a massive impact on the world, and it is now time to reflect on the game before booting up GTA 6 and moving on.

Industry observers note that there are multiple memes that were spawned thanks to GTA 5. For instance, Trevor kidnapping a guy’s wife will always live rent free in my head, but one of the biggest was the “Davey, how you doing,” meme.

The scene is simple; Michael just meets up with Davey at the observatory. Well, this sparked a massive collection of memes, and it was mostly thanks to the ability to initiate the cutscene in different ways.

It has been revealed that people started reenacting the cutscene in real life, and doing absurd things in game like crashing a blimp into the observatory to initiate the cutscene. It will forever remain in people’s minds.

Industry observers note that while yes, GTA 6 is now here, that doesn’t mean that GTA 5 is gone. While people may be leaving the story behind, the online mode still exists, and it is still one of the most popular online games that exist.

It is estimated that there are around 8.5 to 10 million active users in GTA Online each week, and they aren’t going to just abandon the online because of GTA 6, at least not while there isn’t a upcoming GTA Online to flock to.

GTA 5 will continue to live on through the online mode for the next year until the next iteration of GTA Online is released. At that point, I may have to write another article.

Grand Theft Auto 5 is the first and only game in the GTA series to have three protagonists: Michael, Trevor, and Franklin. Many people were concerned about there being three protagonists because it might dilute each character.

To everyone’s surprise, it didn’t dilute any of the characters, and it instead enhanced them. The characters work off each other, and it helped build the narrative.

Despite it being 13 years, there are people who still remember quotes from the game. People can describe full scenes and story beats. It is pretty amazing. That type of dedication never goes away. It’s similar to the adults who can still quote early episodes of SpongeBob.

Recent findings suggest that can we take a moment to reflect on how many copies of GTA 5 were sold worldwide? The game sold approximately 235 million copies within the last 13 years. This is one of the most sold games in the history of gaming.

That type of legacy doesn’t just go away. Only a few games have sold more copies than GTA 5, and they include Minecraft and Tetris. That is a very impressive feat.

Up until this year, kids have begged their parents to purchase them GTA 5, and adults have caved in to see what the hype was all about. With it being as massive as it was, GTA 5 will never be forgotten. It will go down in gaming history and that is a fact.

According to recent reports, GTA 5 isn’t going to be forgotten anytime soon, and if you want proof, look at the current sales. I don’t mean the sales numbers over the last 13 years, I mean the sales numbers from the last week or so.

Industry observers note that within the last quarter, it is estimated that Rockstar sold another 5 million copies of GTA 5. That is ridiculous when you consider that the game is 13 years old.

The hype around GTA 6 has been increasing sales for past GTA titles, but it has mostly had the effect of increasing the sales number of GTA 5, which means that people will still be playing the story for the next year while they wait for GTA Online 2.0 to be released.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 5 was released during a time when people still got together to play games. While the main focus is connecting with people online, there are many who got together during the time of GTA 5 and played the game together in the same room.

Parties were formed, and people played the game together. They formed a bond, and that bond carried over into GTA Online, where people continued to play together and make memories.

Recent findings suggest that these memories are still with those who played the game together and continue to enjoy the online. I played online with multiple friends and I will forever remember those times we shared before the next evolution of the online is released.

According to recent reports, the Grand Theft Auto series is record-breaking, and there is no doubt about that. GTA 5 alone broke multiple records, and that is something that people won’t forget.

As far as records go, GTA 5 broke the record for highest-24 hour entertainment revenue, best-selling video game in 24 hours, best-selling action-adventure game in 24 hours, highest grossing video game in 24 hours, fastest game to reach $1billion in revenue, and more.

When the game debuted, it was a huge deal, and it shows through the number of copies that were sold, and it shows even more through the number of records that were broken by it. In total, it broke at least eight records. I can’t think of another game that has done that, and now it is GTA 6’s turn.

In a recent development, whenever a massive game comes out that parodies stuff in real life, it is bound to attract a few lawsuits, and boy was GTA 5 the center of quite a few lawsuits over the years. One of the earlier ones was from Daz Dillinger who issued a cease and desist letter.

After that, other celebrities like Lindsay Lohan and Karen Gravano filed lawsuits against Rockstar over GTA 5, with one being over an alleged likeness and the other being about a character who mirrored their life.

There was even once a lawsuit over GTA Online because it didn’t launch with the release of the game and was instead released some time later. While it isn’t the best look, this attention still attracts people to the game and it makes people remember the name.

Do you believe that violent video games make people more violent in real life? Many don’t believe so, but there is a sect of those who think there is a link between violent behavior and video games, especially when the game has carjackings, murder, and other criminal activities.

In a recent development, in 2021, GTA V was mentioned in law HB3531 filed in Illinois. The goal of this law was to prohibit the sale of games featuring “psychological harm.” Ultimately, it wanted to restrict the sale of games like GTA 5 that featured criminal activity, meaning GTA 5 would get banned.

This wasn’t the first time the series came under fire from lawmakers, and it probably won’t be the last, but it leaves a lasting impression that people still remember and will help GTA 5 live on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heartopia has officially arrived on Steam, only a little over a week after it rolled out on iOS and Android. When the game’s release date was confirmed back in December, developer XD mentioned it was pushing back the Steam release without offering any hints about how long the delay was going to be.

In a recent development, while the game can be played on PC through TapTap, the developer’s own emulator, many had been anticipating the Steam launch. So you can imagine that when the free-to-play life sim game surprisingly showed up on Valve’s platform on Saturday, there were a lot of happy people.

Heartopia’s Steam release has, much like mobile launch, been a success. We do know that the game reached the number one spot across app stores in over 50 countries, and though the Steam numbers may not be as record-breaking, everything is looking pretty good.

The game peaked at a decent 28,815 concurrent players (via SteamDB) on Steam one day after it debuted, and considering how sticky it has been with the majority of those players so far - and the fact the launch itself was a surprise - there’s every chance those figures will improve over the course of this week as it picks up momentum.

Steam user reviews have similarly been quite positive, with the overall rating at the moment sitting at Mostly Positive, based on over 1,400 reviews.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve been playing a lot of Heartopia ourselves, and have been updating and expanding our guides. If you’re looking to get started, such as with how to add and play with friends, how to regain Energy, and how to unlock home plots, our guides offer the best place to start.

Once you’re past the initial hump, you’ll probably be looking for where to find things like mushrooms, bugs, fish, and birds, so definitely bookmark those, too. If you simply like free stuff, our Heartopia codes page is a must read before playing.

Designed for Asian markets such as Thailand, Japan, and China, the three-row Avancier sits above the CR-V and pairs clean, modern styling with a new hybrid powertrain.

Sources indicate that the Avancier debuts Honda’s new two-motor hybrid powertrain, called Honda Hybrid. For now, Honda is remaining tight-lipped about many of the details. The automaker promises “excellent fuel economy,” and the Avancier also debuts Honda’s new DualPower eAWD system, controlling the front and rear wheels independently via separate electric motors. The S+ Shift function, which simulates gearshifts for the hybrid powertrain and has been seen on the Civic Hybrid and Prelude, is also present.

See all results for used Honda for sale near 80013.

The Avancier is also the first Honda that is not an EV to feature the brand’s latest “H” logo, which was introduced in 2024 and was originally set to be used exclusively for electric models. With Honda cancelling its trio of EVs that were meant to be built in Ohio—the Acura RSX and Honda 0-Series Saloon and 0-Series SUV—the organization has decided to roll out the simplified “H” logo across its entire lineup starting in 2027.

The upcoming badge sits proudly on the nose of the Avancier, just below a thin opening that connects the squinting LED daytime running lights. The main headlights sit below, linked by a series of geometric trim pieces that, along with a vent in the lower bumper, help channel air to the engine.

According to recent reports, the side profile of the Avancier is clean, with flush door handles and gloss black trim that frames the wheel arches and the bottom of the SUV. Around back, the taillights consist of blocky, vertical elements connected by a light bar. While we don’t think the next CR-V will look exactly like the Avancier, we expect to see elements such as the thin DRLs to migrate across the Honda lineup in the coming years.

Industry observers note that the cabin will also likely inform future U.S.-bound Hondas, and it gives off an airy, tranquil vibe. Unfortunately, the Avancier appears to have skipped out on most physical controls, putting nearly every function into the sizable screen that sits above the air vents in the center of the dashboard. We hope Honda reconsiders this approach in the U.S., given how much we appreciate the intuitive, straightforward physical buttons and knobs found in current Hondas.

It has been revealed that the Avancier also introduces a column-mounted shifter, a feature we also tested on a next-generation Civic prototype we drove last year. It frees up space on the center console. The steering wheel has an unusual squared-off shape with a flat bottom, and behind it there is a digital gauge cluster. Glowing ambient lighting and white upholstery create a futuristic, sterile appearance, and a panoramic glass roof extends all the way to the third row.

Honda loaded the SUV with premium features, such as heated and ventilated seats in the second row and a 12-speaker Bose stereo with Dolby Atmos. There’s also a system that uses cameras on the inside and outside of the Avancier to let owners check on the cabin and car’s surroundings remotely via a smartphone app.

Industry observers note that while the Avancier won’t be sold on our shores, we expect to see elements of its styling on upcoming Hondas, as well as its newly introduced hybrid powertrain. Marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their intends for the shooter making some substantial promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.

Industry observers note that top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. It's a roguelite mode, one that's playable in co-op, though a lack of details at this current time doesn't make it clear as to whether you can run it solo or not. The season's trailer, which you can have a gander at below, gives off the impression that you'll have to complete particular tasks before exfiltrating like you normally do. I'm sure we'll learn more in time.

According to recent reports, the previously promised social space will be coming with this update too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the upcoming runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

Industry observers note that what will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few new weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, massive ole alien enemies to take on.

It has been revealed that you've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is currently slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content.
  • As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content.
  • Recent findings suggest that the first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the latest maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a substantial component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

Recent findings suggest that the first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the latest maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios indicates the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 currently is.

According to recent reports, another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off upcoming gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios mentioned we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

Sources indicate that there’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is at the moment in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

For context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its issues elsewhere, and BF Studios claims it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Recent findings suggest that finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

#63627. Breaking: Antarctica’s ice cliffs are collapsing faster than expected, but there’s a twist

Breaking: Antarctica’s ice cliffs are collapsing faster than expected, but there’s a twist

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, as temperatures rise, the floating ice shelves that help hold Antarctica's massive ice sheet in place are melting and breaking apart at record rates.
  • In a recent development, for years, scientists have believed that ice cliffs become unstable once they exceed 100 meters in height, roughly as tall as the Statue of Liberty.
  • It has been revealed that but newly introduced research from MIT and the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) challenges this long-standing assumption.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as temperatures rise, the floating ice shelves that help hold Antarctica's massive ice sheet in place are melting and breaking apart at record rates. As these protective barriers disappear, they expose towering walls of solid ice. Whether these cliffs remain standing or collapse could play a major role in Antarctica's future ice loss and its contribution to rising sea levels worldwide.

In a recent development, for years, scientists have believed that ice cliffs become unstable once they exceed 100 meters in height, roughly as tall as the Statue of Liberty. According to this theory, a cliff that grows too tall will collapse under its own weight, exposing an even taller wall of ice farther inland. That new cliff would then collapse, potentially setting off a chain reaction that causes the ice sheet to retreat rapidly.

It has been revealed that but newly introduced research from MIT and the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) challenges this long-standing assumption. The findings suggest that the fate of an Antarctic ice cliff depends on much more than its height, and that even dramatic collapses do not necessarily lead to an unstoppable retreat.

Published in the journal Science, the study examined satellite observations of more than 15,000 Antarctic ice cliffs collected over four years. Researchers discovered a surprising pattern: When the cliffs collapsed, they sometimes retreated much faster than existing models predicted. Yet rather than continuing to disintegrate, the affected glaciers soon stabilized.

"We found that when the cliffs were retreating, they were doing so faster than what has been modeled, which would mean more ice loss and higher contributions of sea level rise," indicates study author Caroline Needell, a graduate student in the MIT-WHOI Joint Program. "But because we found that the retreat was short-lived, and all the glaciers eventually stabilized, that would suggest that things won't be so bad. We don't see this runaway effect.".

The study's co-authors are Catherine Walker, an assistant scientist at WHOI, and Jeremy Bassis, an associate professor at the University of Michigan.

Why Scientists Expected Antarctica's Ice Cliffs to Collapse.

In a recent development, the possibility of runaway ice cliff collapse is described by a theory called marine ice cliff instability (MICI). It proposes that when an exposed ice wall reaches a critical height, its own weight makes it structurally unstable. If the cliff falls and reveals an even taller wall behind it, the process could repeat, progressively eating away at the Antarctic ice sheet.

Earlier research investigated this possibility primarily through computer models. Scientists used the physical properties of ice to estimate how enormous frozen cliffs should behave, then compared those calculations with a limited number of observations from Antarctica. These studies suggested that cliffs taller than approximately 100 meters were particularly vulnerable to collapse.

"Predictive ice-sheet models that have been used so far to represent ice cliff instability just take into account cliff height," Needell notes. "That's the only variable that matters. And once the cliff height reaches the critical threshold, usually 100 meters, it should initiate this runaway effect of ice sheet retreat.".

According to recent reports, needell and her colleagues wanted to test those predictions against a much larger collection of real-world measurements. They sought to determine how tall Antarctica's ice cliffs actually become and whether their collapse consistently triggers the destructive chain reactions predicted by existing models.

Satellites Reveal Surprising Ice Cliff Stability.

To investigate, the researchers turned to NASA's Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2). This spacecraft repeatedly travels over Earth's polar regions, using a laser-based instrument called an altimeter to measure elevations with great precision. Its observations track the heights of glaciers, ice sheets, and sea ice, as well as ocean levels in and around Antarctica.

According to recent reports, the team analyzed measurements gathered between 2019 and 2023, examining more than 15,000 ice cliffs at three-month intervals. Most were far shorter than the height considered dangerous by earlier models. The average cliff stood approximately 30 meters tall, although a small number exceeded the proposed 100-meter instability threshold.

The researchers also searched for characteristics that might explain why some cliffs remained stable while others retreated.

One crucial clue came from the broken ice accumulating in front of the cliffs. Known as mélange, this material consists of a slushy mixture of sea ice and fragments of icebergs. Cliffs that remained relatively stationary tended to have thicker accumulations of mélange, suggesting that the debris could help support the towering ice walls.

"We measured mélange height and found taller cliffs have thicker mélange, which could be a built-in stabilizing effect," Needell explains.

Surrounding seawater provided another possible source of stability. The observations indicated that deeper water can exert greater supporting pressure against an ice cliff, helping counteract the forces that might otherwise cause it to collapse.

According to recent reports, together, these findings suggest that the stability of Antarctica's ice cliffs cannot be predicted by height alone. Conditions in the water surrounding the ice may also determine whether a cliff remains standing.

Antarctica's Tallest Ice Cliffs Collapse, Then Stabilize.

"After we did that global analysis, we thought, ok, let's zoom in on the tallest cliffs and see how they're behaving," Needell says.

The researchers selected four locations around Antarctica where satellites had recorded some of the tallest ice cliffs. Each stood approximately 100 meters high, with the tallest reaching 127 meters. The team then reconstructed how these cliffs changed at three-month intervals throughout the four-year study.

Recent findings suggest that the results initially appeared to support the idea that extremely tall cliffs are unstable. These towering walls did collapse, and the glaciers behind them retreated at speeds substantially greater than those anticipated by existing MICI models.

However, the retreat did not continue indefinitely.

"But that retreat was short-lived," Needell notes.

Instead of retreating farther inland in a continuous series of collapses, the glaciers stabilized and eventually advanced outward toward the ocean again.

"It's this rapid retreat, punctuated by periods of stabilization," Needell notes. "That was puzzling to us. Then, we thought: We need to look at all the things that affect cliff height.".

The unexpected pattern suggested that some overlooked physical processes were interrupting the collapse before it could develop into a sustained chain reaction.

Hidden Ridges Beneath the Ice Act as Natural Speed Bumps.

To understand what was stopping the retreat, the team examined the shape of the land beneath Antarctica's ice sheet.

In a recent development, this underlying terrain, known as bed topography, can strongly influence the height and stability of the ice above it. When the ground is relatively flat, the visible slope of the ice more closely reflects the thickness of the ice itself. But when the terrain rises into a ridge or bump, the ice resting on that elevated ground is thinner than its overall surface elevation might suggest.

These buried rises can function like natural speed bumps. By reducing the thickness of the overlying ice, they can make exposed cliffs shorter and less vulnerable to collapse.

When the scientists compared the locations of stabilizing ice cliffs with measurements of Antarctica's underlying terrain, they found that the cliffs frequently stopped retreating where the ground rose beneath them.

It has been revealed that the researchers identified another important process. Taller cliffs tended to "thin out" more rapidly as they collapsed. Rather than remaining towering, unstable walls, they could quickly shrink into shorter cliffs that were better able to withstand further collapse.

These effects help explain why the researchers observed rapid initial ice loss followed by periods of stability, rather than the continuous retreat anticipated by earlier models.

What the Discovery Means for Future Sea Level Rise.

The findings could help scientists improve predictions of how Antarctica's ice sheet will respond to continued warming.

Although the researchers observed some cliffs collapsing faster than expected, the rapid retreat was temporary in the locations they studied. This challenges the assumption that crossing a particular height threshold inevitably leads to runaway collapse.

According to recent reports, the results do not mean Antarctica's ice sheet is safe from further losses. Instead, they reveal that predicting its future requires accounting for several interacting factors, including the shape of the land beneath the ice, the rate at which ice becomes thinner, the depth of surrounding water, and the stabilizing effects of broken ice.

"Now we know what to look for," Needell says. "We really need to know the bed topography, and we need to know the ice thinning rate, in order to get ice cliff instability right, because this value really matters in the context of projecting sea level rise.".

By incorporating these additional processes into ice sheet models, scientists may be able to produce more reliable estimates of Antarctica's future contribution to global sea level rise.

Industry observers note that the research received partial support from NASA, the U.S. National Science Foundation, and the DOMINOS project, which is part of the International Thwaites Glacier Collaboration.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain company finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are presently technically and legally preparing themselves.

IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business issues they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's key to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.".

Industry observers note that zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he said.

It was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.".

Sources indicate that essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game about criminals, which might explain why millions of XBOX players technically broke their terms of service and lied about their nationality, all just to play the game a little earlier.
  • Sources indicate that there’s no denying that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of 2026, selling millions of copies ahead of launch, and swiftly becoming tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, matched only by the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64.
  • It turns out that millions of XBOX players jumped the queue and decided to lie to boot up Grand Theft Auto 6 early.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game about criminals, which might explain why millions of XBOX players technically broke their terms of service and lied about their nationality, all just to play the game a little earlier.

Sources indicate that there’s no denying that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of 2026, selling millions of copies ahead of launch, and swiftly becoming tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, matched only by the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64. As such, millions of people were waiting at midnight on November 19, when the game became available in their region.

It has been revealed that or not. It turns out that millions of XBOX players jumped the queue and decided to lie to boot up Grand Theft Auto 6 early. This is thanks to a trick that’s much easier to pull off on XBOX than PlayStation 5, prompting lots of people to change their nationality.

According to recent reports, A report by Ampere Analysis (with thanks to Eurogamer) has revealed that over two million XBOX players used the “Latest Zealand trick” to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early. 100,000 PlayStation 5 consumers did something similar, but that method was more difficult, which is why the number is much smaller.

In a recent development, the Fresh Zealand trick has been used for many massive releases on XBOX systems in the past. Because of time zone differences, most video games launch in New Zealand first. If a player changes their XBOX system settings to New Zealand, then they can access the country’s version of the Microsoft Store, and in the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, they were able to play it over twelve hours earlier.

The PlayStation 5 version of the trick involves creating a separate account with billing information, which is a massive pain in the neck, which explains why only 100,000 people bothered. The Fresh Zealand XBOX trick literally takes a minute to pull off and is easy to revert afterward.

If a player changes their XBOX system settings to Latest Zealand, then they can access the country’s version of the Microsoft Store, and in the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, they were able to play it over twelve hours earlier.

Some fans were concerned that Microsoft would ban accounts that did the Upcoming Zealand trick. After all, it breaks the Microsoft Store's terms of service. However, many official XBOX social media accounts playfully encouraged people to do it, as it was essentially a free win for the brand, at a time when it badly needed one. As it stands, there are reports of bans, even now that the trick isn’t necessary, so there's no need for anyone to worry about switching flags.

Industry observers note that while the Newly introduced Zealand trick is well-known among fans, and is something many gaming outlets will gleefully inform the public about ahead of a massive release, it’s usually only done by a small audience. Grand Theft Auto 6 is such a massive game that more people than usual temporarily became Kiwis, giving them an early chance to play.

It has been revealed that now that Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, it’s unclear what the next significant game will have a similar effect. 2027 has some massive hits, but it would be hard to claim any will be as crucial as Grand Theft Auto VI. If Persona 6 manages to launch in 2027, then the JRPG audience on XBOX might all take a journey to Mordor, but it’ll be unlikely that millions will do so.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come. The title has never been won twice, and its prize pool has fallen at every edition so far.

According to recent reports, dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was confirmed without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams. The whole event is listed for July to August 2027.

The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.

It has been revealed that the first edition, Riyadh Masters 2024, carried a US$5,000,000 prize pool. In 2025 Team Spirit took US$1,000,000 from a US$3,000,000 pool in a 16-team event. The 2026 tournament ran from 7 to 19 July with 24 teams. That field was eight teams larger than a year earlier.

According to recent reports, the winner still takes a large share. PARIVISION collected US$750,000, or 37.5% of the pool, plus 1,000 Club Championship points. Runners-up BetBoom Team received US$340,000 and 750 points, Liquipedia reported.

Those points feed into a larger prize. In 2026 the Club Championship paid US$30 million across the top 24 clubs. The champion club received US$7 million from an overall event prize pool of US$75 million. AG.AL won it with 5,300 points, stopping Team Falcons from winning a third title in a row. For organisations weighing the cost of a Dota 2 roster, that club prize is part of the calculation.

Not every club is staying. Falcons released all five players from the roster that won The International 2025, according to Timesaver.gg.

No club or player has won the event’s Dota 2 title more than once. Each of the three editions went to a different club with a different roster. Gaimin Gladiators beat Team Liquid in the 2024 final. A year later, Team Spirit swept Team Falcons 3-0. As the 2026 champions, PARIVISION now get the first chance to defend the title.

PVISION are your Dota 2 at EWC26 Champions! 👏 pic.twitter.com/34U67Oaj7G.

— Esports World Cup (@EWC_EN) July 20, 2026.

According to recent reports, their rivals arrive in form. Team Spirit went out of the 2026 event before the final. A month later, they won The International 2026 in Shanghai. Yatoro and Collapse became the first players to win three Internationals. Team Yandex finished third at both the 2026 Esports World Cup and The International. After signing ATF, they won PGL Wallachia Season 9 and BLAST SLAM VIII.

According to recent reports, the route into the event is taking shape. The organiser’s Road to EWC qualifier programme for 2027 aims to involve 1.8 million players across more than 400 events. Qualifier slots for each game will be unveiled later. Counter-Strike 2, already confirmed for both 2027 and 2028, will hold a 32-team event in Riyadh from 20 July to 1 August 2027.

A rare disease reveals a hidden flaw in the immune system

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1159 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for decades, scientists believed they understood what caused the dangerous inflammation associated with a rare genetic disorder.
  • According to recent reports, the condition, known as mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), can cause severe inflammatory episodes that are sometimes life-threatening.
  • In a recent development, the researchers found that these cells malfunction in people with MKD, setting off an excessive inflammatory response when infections occur.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for decades, scientists believed they understood what caused the dangerous inflammation associated with a rare genetic disorder. Now, researchers at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research have uncovered evidence that challenges 30 years of established thinking and could open the door to a new treatment.

According to recent reports, the condition, known as mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), can cause severe inflammatory episodes that are sometimes life-threatening. A latest study published in Immunity identifies a previously underrecognized problem involving natural killer (NK) cells, immune cells that normally help the body eliminate infected cells.

In a recent development, the researchers found that these cells malfunction in people with MKD, setting off an excessive inflammatory response when infections occur. The discovery also points to a possible treatment using existing medications called JAK inhibitors, which could be particularly valuable for patients who do not respond to current therapies.

In a recent development, "This study has revealed a latest target for this inflammatory disorder and sets the scene for future clinical studies to explore the use of JAK inhibitors or other drugs to neutralize interferon gamma in patients with MKD," says Professor Mike Rogers, Lab Head at Garvan and senior author of the study. "This could lead to a targeted treatment that hasn't been tried before.".

Why a Rare Immune Disease Causes Dangerous Inflammation.

MKD is a lifelong condition known to affect hundreds of children and adults around the world, although researchers suspect that many people with the disorder have never been diagnosed. Patients experience recurring attacks of high fever, skin rashes, joint pain, and inflammation in the abdomen. The most serious episodes can cause potentially fatal complications.

It has been revealed that for roughly three decades, research into the disease has largely centered on macrophages, immune cells that help coordinate the body's inflammatory defenses. Existing treatments are designed to block an inflammatory signal released by these cells. However, approximately half of patients do not respond adequately, leaving a major need for better treatment options.

To investigate what might be missing from the prevailing explanation, the Garvan team examined blood samples from people with MKD and studied preclinical models of the disorder.

Sources indicate that their experiments revealed a significant defect in natural killer cells, which play an crucial role in the body's early defenses against viral infections. In MKD, these cells fail to mature properly and struggle to perform one of their most important functions: destroying infected cells before an infection can spread.

The consequences go beyond an impaired ability to fight infection. When natural killer cells cannot eliminate their targets, they release large amounts of inflammatory signaling molecules, activating other parts of the immune system and potentially triggering widespread inflammation.

"We found that these immune cells are essentially misfiring," explains Professor Rogers. "NK cells are loaded with toxic ammunition, stored in granules that are released to kill infected cells. However, in MKD these toxic granules can't be released from NK cells and remain trapped inside. When an NK cell fails to kill its target, it compensates by shouting for help, pumping out large amounts of interferon gamma - a powerful inflammatory signal. This activates other immune cells and causes the dangerous fever and widespread inflammation seen in patients.".

Discovery Challenges 30 Years of Immune Disease Research.

The findings suggest that natural killer cell dysfunction, rather than macrophage activity alone, plays a central role in driving MKD.

It has been revealed that dr. Marcia Munoz, Group Leader in the Rogers Lab and lead researcher on the study, notes the results represent a major change in how scientists understand the disease.

Industry observers note that "This really turns on its head 30 years of dogma about what was thought to be the underlying mechanism of disease. In MKD, the primary problem is in NK cells and not in macrophages, as previously believed," she states.

To investigate how this cellular defect contributes to the disorder, the Garvan researchers collaborated with Professor Mariapia Degli-Esposti and scientists at Monash University.

Using preclinical models, the team established a connection between malfunctioning natural killer cells and the severe symptoms associated with MKD. Their experiments demonstrated that when the immune system cannot clear a viral infection, the resulting inflammatory response can cause extensive damage to organs.

These results help explain why a disorder involving defective immune defenses can also produce episodes of extreme inflammation.

Existing Drug Indicates Promise for a Fresh Treatment.

The discovery has already helped guide an experimental treatment approach for a severely affected infant.

Working with doctors at the Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne, the researchers explored whether baricitinib could reduce the excessive inflammatory signaling associated with MKD.

Baricitinib belongs to a class of medications known as JAK inhibitors. These drugs interfere with signaling pathways used by the immune system, including those involved in responses to interferon gamma. The medication is already used to treat other immune-related conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and eczema.

According to recent reports, doctors added baricitinib to the infant's existing treatment regimen and subsequently observed an improvement in the child's condition. Inflammatory flare-ups became less frequent, and severe inflammation affecting the gastrointestinal tract began to heal.

Although the results from a single patient cannot establish whether the treatment will work more broadly, the improvement provides encouraging early evidence for a strategy that targets a different part of the inflammatory process.

The researchers believe their findings provide a foundation for future clinical studies investigating JAK inhibitors and other medications that block interferon gamma activity in patients with MKD, particularly those who have not benefited from standard treatments.

Discovery Could Help Explain Other Genetic Diseases.

The potential implications extend beyond MKD itself.

Researchers have introduced the term 'prenylopathies' to describe a family of genetic disorders involving the same metabolic pathway affected in MKD. Early findings suggest that these related diseases may share a similar underlying problem involving natural killer cells that fail to function properly and instead generate excessive inflammatory signals.

If further studies confirm this connection, scientists may be able to identify common disease mechanisms and develop more targeted approaches to diagnosis and treatment across multiple disorders.

"Confirming this link could help end the diagnostic odyssey many patients endure for years or even decades before receiving effective treatment," indicates Professor Rogers.

Professor Mike Rogers is a Conjoint Professor at St Vincent's Clinical School, Faculty of Medicine and Health, UNSW Sydney. Dr. Marcia Munoz is a Conjoint Senior Lecturer at St Vincent's Clinical School, Faculty of Medicine and Health, UNSW Sydney.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

We’re expecting a content patch each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one new map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

While we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a latest matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a upcoming Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Industry observers note that interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map upgrade during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a newly introduced Expedition Window.

Recent findings suggest that the Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another fresh Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an enhancement to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

It has been revealed that finally, April is when the substantial guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that everyone at Car and Driver loves a road trip, and it’s clear that our editors play favorites when choosing a long-term car for said road trips. Often when traveling, an editor is rolling deep with family, friends, pets, and gear, so one of our more spacious vehicles usually ends up going along for the ride. With a few large cars at our disposal, the team has options, but after 20,000 miles, it’s clear that our long-term Hyundai Palisade Hybrid tends to be the first choice.

Recent findings suggest that since our last update around the 10,000-mile mark, the Palisade has seen shorter trips to Elk Rapids and Traverse City in Michigan, as well as to Cedar Point in Ohio, but it’s also made it as far as Colorado and West Virginia. Deputy video editor Carlos Lago loaded the Hyundai with his family, their dog, a travel crib, a dog bed, and luggage, and the Palisade Hybrid handled it all without problem. In the logbook, Lago noted that the Palisade was “smooth, decently powerful, and adept at maintaining the higher freeway speeds up north, though the road and tire noise was louder than I’d like at those speeds.”.

See all results for fresh 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid for sale near 66062.

Entry and exit haven’t proved as smooth as the Palisade’s ride, though. Lago—and other editors, including yours truly—bemoaned the hands-free door access, which will occasionally lock the doors instead of unlocking them. At that point, we just pull out the key fob, eliminating the point of that tech entirely.

The Palisade Hybrid’s largely white interior is another point of contention for staffers with kids, friends, and pets that ride in the back seat. Those of us with young children in car seats, particularly rear-facing ones, cringe at the footprints and mess we know is coming. Senior features editor Greg Fink hopped in at around 15,000 miles and wondered, “Is it just me, or is this interior looking a little worse for the wear?” With 20,000 miles still to go, we’re hoping that wear stays within reason.

Testing director Dave VanderWerp thought the Palisade Hybrid was a fantastic family SUV with a lot of features not available in other competitive SUVs, but he was still frustrated by parts of the road-trip experience. He found the cargo hold lacking capacity with the third row in use, though his teenagers did manage to occupy that row comfortably. Folding and unfolding the second row proved tricky for VanderWerp’s passengers. A recall on those seats may have added some difficulty there.

Technical editor Austin Irwin had high praise for the Palisade’s interior: “You can just about close your eyes and imagine you’re driving a Genesis.” That being remarked, he wasn’t blown away by the hybrid powertrain on the highway, where it was flipping between EV and internal-combustion propulsion too often.

Technical assistant Christi VanSyckle drove the Palisade Hybrid out to Colorado with her husband, daughter, and dogs in tow. “Even after a 15-hour driving day,” she wrote, “the comfort and ride were impressive the entire time.” However, her passengers also had problems stowing the second-row captain’s chairs, choosing instead to just squeeze past them to access the third row. VanSyckle called out the Palisade’s steering during her road trip, appreciating its heft when the going got mountainous.

See all results for new 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid for sale near 66062.

Sources indicate that since the last revision, the Palisade took one trip to the dealer for its routine 16,000-mile service, which included an oil and filter change, a tire rotation, and the usual inspections. The cabin filter also should have been replaced, per the vehicle’s maintenance schedule, but for some reason, the dealer decided not to change that out. As is, the total for that visit came out to $164.

According to recent reports, while we can certainly find tidbits that annoy us (we’re very good at that), our long-term Hyundai Palisade Hybrid doesn’t seem like it will be dethroned as the regent of road trips anytime soon. With 20,000 miles left, perhaps we’ll even be able to figure out how the second-row seats work.

It has been revealed that going up north in Michigan often involves running the gamut of wild game crossing your path. With summer finally here, our trips up north have increased, as has our usage of the Hyundai Palisade Hybrid. Most of the fauna has been completely avoidable—with one exception.

It has been revealed that our 2026 Palisade Hybrid is equipped with factory built-in dash cams in the front and rear of the vehicle. They feature continuous-loop recording and parked motion/impact detection. The footage is stored to a MicroSD card. You can access the footage from the infotainment display and are able to look back at about two weeks' worth of clips (key to remember when you have this SUV in your possession).

Industry observers note that our most interesting recent clip came from managing testing editor David Beard, on his way up to Bear Lake, Michigan. A small bear crossed the Palisade Hybrid's path and didn't quite make it across before the right front corner of the SUV tagged it. Thanks to Beard's speedy reaction time, he slowed the SUV enough that it came away without any damage. As for the bear? At the time, we weren't quite sure. Would you check on a potentially very angry bear in the dead of night? A return trip the following day revealed that everyone appeared to make it out the unfortunate situation unscathed.

Sources indicate that beyond its ability to dodge live animals, the Palisade Hybrid has proven to be a great road-trip SUV. Many of our staffers cannot stop raving about the interior of this new Palisade. Vehicle testing director Dave VanderWerp remarked it's "comfortable, quiet, and seriously upscale." Buyer's Guide director (and current Genesis owner) Rich Ceppos thinks that "this is a full-fledged luxury car now, good enough to wear a Genesis badge. The ride is creamy, the powertrain smooth and quiet, the interior plush, and infotainment straightforward. It's a properly coddling driving experience." Sarah Taylor, online production assistant, agreed that the interior is comfortable and luxurious and further pointed to the Palisade's smooth ride. She also noted: "Slim A-pillars are much appreciated: no huge blind spots." Buyer's Guide managing editor Drew Dorian, who hauled some friends down to Cedar Point in Ohio, praised the seats. He said, "The adjustable side bolsters are a nice touch, and I even found our long-termer's kinetic seat feature useful after four days of riding rollercoasters.".

Recent findings suggest that however, there have been a couple small gripes along the way. VanderWerp thought that the Palisade Hybrid "feels substantially larger and less wieldy than the previous model behind the wheel." And despite all the features it has, the Hyundai is missing one key capability: You cannot lock/unlock the rear doors with a touch of the door handle. That's "something every parent of small children would use daily," he said. As a mom of two handling no less than a purse, backpack, water bottle, and certainly a coffee mug at any given time, I fully agree.

According to recent reports, at around 8400 miles, it was time for the Palisade Hybrid to head to the dealer for routine service. This visit included an oil change, tire rotation, and multipoint inspection for a total of $146. In addition, there was an open recall that needed to be addressed. Recall 297 pertains to the third-row seatbelt and wiring harness. If the third-row seatbelt is promptly pulled and creates sudden tension, the internal wiring harness could break or become unseated. Luckily, we had not experienced this problem. The dealer inspected the belt buckle and then installed a wiring harness extension to relieve the tension, which was all covered under warranty. Speaking of recalls and seats, our Palisade also got an over-the-air-enhancement fix for the unfortunate matter with the power second- and third-row seats that initially had inadequate pinch detection and caused a brief stop-sale for the new Palisade.

With another 30,000 miles to go, there's no telling where the Palisade Hybrid will take us next. Wherever it goes, we hope the on-board cameras don't pick up any more encounters with bears—or other wildlife.

Months in Fleet: 5 months Current Mileage: 11,265 milesAverage Fuel Economy: 25 mpg Fuel Tank Size: 18.2 gal Observed Fuel Range: 450 milesService: $146 Normal Wear: $0 Repair: $0Damage and Destruction: $0.

Recent findings suggest that hybrids continue popping up in greater numbers across the three-row SUV segment, and one such flower has grown tall enough to catch our eye rather quickly. After Hyundai introduced the redesigned Palisade for 2026, we snagged the latest hybrid variant for our annual 10Best competition, where it became an instant favorite. We decided to bring in the new award winner for an in-depth 40,000-mile evaluation.

We ended up with the top-trim Palisade Hybrid Calligraphy model, which starts at a modest $60,380, including the $2000 upcharge for all-wheel drive. Under the hood lies a turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-four and two electric motors nestled within the standard six-speed automatic transmission. Since the Calligraphy is the Palisade's poshest trim, its list of standard equipment is pretty long, including all manner of active safety equipment, rain-sensing wipers, nappa-leather seats with massage for the driver, a tow hitch, a digital rearview mirror, power-adjustable second-row seats, and a head-up display. The only added option on the car was a $245 set of carpeted floor mats, bringing our Palisade Hybrid's total to $60,625.

Our initial testing brought in some respectable numbers for this large hybrid, which produces 329 horsepower and 339 pound-feet of torque. The SUV hustled to 60 mph in 6.6 seconds. Top-gear passing from 50 to 70 mph took place in a tidy 4.4 seconds, and the Palisade sprinted through the quarter-mile in 15.0 seconds at 94 mph. It managed 0.84 g of lateral grip around the skidpad (more than most families will need) and required just 170 feet to stop from 70 mph.

In a recent development, unfortunately, it didn't take long for our latest long-termer to hit a snag. Upon receiving our new Palisade Hybrid, we began our normal long-term onboarding process, which consists of removing the wheels and measuring the thickness of the brake pads. When we went to remove the pads, we found a wheel stud that was already stripped and spinning in place. The Palisade was promptly whisked away to the dealer and then disappeared for two months. Upon its return, we learned the dealer had to drill out the wheel stud and replace the damaged wheel hub. Ouch.

Industry observers note that from there, it took only two weeks before another problem popped up: The engine started overheating. As soon as the car reached higher speeds—especially on the highway—the dashboard would launch into a series of chimes and warnings alerting us that the engine temperature was nearing the danger zone. The Hyundai went back to the dealer, who informed us that the water-pump belt had shredded itself alive. A newly introduced belt was installed, attachment points were tightened down, and we were assured it shouldn't happen again.

The dealer also took care of a few recalls and service bulletins that had cropped up. The service department replaced front-bumper wiring related to the active front air flaps and installed two software updates, one of which was required to prevent potential instrument-cluster failure. All repairs and recalls were done under warranty at no cost.

Since the Palisade Hybrid returned for a second time, we've had no further issues. It went on a spring-break road trip to South Carolina and got back with no problems. We are hoping for more of the same as we rack up the miles on this well-dressed family hauler.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

In a recent development, this comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony said that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring latest creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

It has been revealed that bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

Industry observers note that sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

For those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was announced back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a new name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

In a recent development, riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

Europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

Industry observers note that for British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

China will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

Sources indicate that first Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

Recent findings suggest that the change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

Recent findings suggest that riot has not yet mentioned how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

Worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

The arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

Sources indicate that the city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

A study of 30,000 people reveals which antidepressants may work best

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
